market_background.ecological_environment_code: Effective 2026-08-15, establishes comprehensive auto-monitoring and self-monitoring obligations for all pollution permit holders. Key change: all key permit holders must install, network, and maintain auto-monitoring equipment with video surveillance.
market_background.environmental_monitoring_regulation: Effective 2026-01-01, establishes legal framework for monitoring data quality and enterprise primary responsibility.
market_background.hj_1480_2026: New technical standard for self-monitoring video surveillance system construction and networking, published Jul 2026.
market_background.zld_trend: Multiple ZLD projects in thermal power (desulfurization wastewater) and battery (production wastewater) industries indicate continued regulatory push for zero discharge.
market_background.pharmaceutical_wastewater: Complex pharmaceutical wastewater treatment remains challenging - 70%+ of projects experience commissioning delays per industry analysis.

source_effectiveness.government_websites: High effectiveness for compliance signals - official Code text, provincial/municipal implementation letters
source_effectiveness.tender_platforms: Medium effectiveness for CapEx signals - qianlima, ccgp, okcis provide project-level details but often mask company names
source_effectiveness.industry_media: Medium - bjx.com.cn effective for power industry water treatment projects
source_effectiveness.gaps: Semiconductor UPW projects not found in public tenders - likely procured through private channels. Food & beverage industry signals weak this cycle.

experiment_observations.municipal_vs_industrial_differentiation: Industrial radar successfully differentiated from municipal by focusing on: (1) enterprise-level compliance obligations vs municipal utility obligations, (2) process water treatment vs municipal wastewater, (3) ZLD/UPW specialty systems vs municipal treatment. No municipal WWTP or water supply projects included.

demand_learning_summary.new_strong_pull: Ecological Environment Code compliance (PULL 15/20) is the strongest demand signal discovered. It is a cross-sector regulatory forcing function affecting all key pollution discharge permit holders. However, it is a regulatory-level signal, not enterprise-specific - requires further work to identify specific enterprises with monitoring gaps.
demand_learning_summary.repeatable_patterns: Two repeatable patterns identified: (1) ZLD water treatment projects in thermal power and battery industries - recurring environmental requirement but iMS leverage is limited to lifecycle/installed base; (2) Code compliance-driven auto-monitoring upgrades - cross-sector but needs enterprise-level qualification.
demand_learning_summary.downgraded_signals: Feida wastewater system procurement (PULL 6/20) downgraded to REJECT - no clear project/pain/forcing function for iMS. Tongling chemical park self-monitoring (PULL 10/20) downgraded to REJECT - tender is for third-party testing service, not instrumentation/iMS.
demand_learning_summary.gtm_assessment: The Code compliance signal suggests a potentially larger TAM than single-project water systems - all key pollution permit holders need monitoring upgrades. This may warrant a GTM strategy targeting compliance-driven instrument networking and data management, rather than only project-level water system opportunities.

repeatable_demand_signals.pattern: ZLD/Zero Liquid Discharge water treatment projects
repeatable_demand_signals.instances: 3 signals (50GWh battery, Dalian thermal power, Shishi thermal power)

repeatable_demand_signals.ims_relevance: Medium - ZLD systems need instrument monitoring, but primary procurement is EPC total package. iMS fit is lifecycle/installed base rather than new procurement.

repeatable_demand_signals.pattern: Ecological Environment Code compliance-driven auto-monitoring upgrade
repeatable_demand_signals.demand_signature: Legal mandate forcing all key pollution permit holders to install/network auto-monitoring equipment
repeatable_demand_signals.ims_relevance: High potential - iMS can provide compliance dashboard, data networking, anomaly alerting. But need to identify specific enterprises with gaps.

experiment_observations.methodology_evaluation: Week 4 assessment: Engine A (compliance) discovered stronger demand signals (Code enforcement) than Engine B (CapEx) this cycle. Engine B signals are mostly EPC total packages where instrument procurement is locked within EPC, limiting iMS leverage. PULL framework successfully prevented over-qualification of EPC-bound signals. Key gap: semiconductor and food & beverage industries underrepresented this cycle.
experiment_observations.pull_framework_validation: PULL v1 framework effectively filtered out signals where iMS cannot change Decision/Action/Outcome. 2 REJECT decisions made based on insufficient demand evidence despite industry relevance. No signals forced to PASS based on iMS feature match alone.
